subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a plant with two colours of arrows (or describe them): one for water and minerals, one for food. Show where each starts and ends.
prompt_hi: Do rang ke teer wala paudha banao (ya batao): ek paani aur minerals ke liye, ek khaane ke liye. Dikhaao har ek kahaan se shuru aur kahaan khatam hota hai.
answer: Water arrows: from roots up the stem to the leaves (xylem). Food arrows: from leaves to buds, flowers, fruits upward and to roots or tubers downward (phloem).

subject: science
prompt_en: A potted plant's leaves droop on a hot afternoon even though the soil is a little moist. Explain using transpiration and water transport.
prompt_hi: Garam dopahar mein gamle ke paudhe ke patte murjha jaate hain jabki mitti thodi geeli hai. Transpiration aur paani ke transport se samjhao.
answer: In heat, leaves lose water by transpiration faster than roots can absorb and xylem can supply it, so cells lose water and the leaves droop; they usually recover in the evening.

subject: science
prompt_en: A giant banyan or a tall coconut tree has no pump, yet water reaches leaves many metres up. Explain how.
prompt_hi: Bade bargad ya oonche naariyal ke ped mein koi pump nahi hota, phir bhi paani kai meter upar patton tak pahunch jaata hai. Samjhao kaise.
answer: Water evaporates from the leaves through stomata (transpiration), and this creates a pull that draws a continuous column of water up through the narrow xylem tubes from the roots.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how the water you pour on a tulsi plant reaches its top leaves, and how the food made in the leaves reaches its roots.
prompt_hi: Chhote bachche ko samjhao ki tulsi pe daala hua paani upar ke patton tak kaise pahunchta hai, aur patton mein bana khaana jadon tak kaise.
answer: Key ideas: roots absorb water and minerals; xylem carries them up; transpiration from leaves helps pull water up; leaves make food; phloem carries food to all parts, including the roots.

subject: science
prompt_en: From memory: what are the tiny hair-like outgrowths on roots that absorb water called?
prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: jadon ke woh chhote baal jaise ubhaar jo paani sokhte hain, kya kehlaate hain?
answer: Root hairs.

subject: science
prompt_en: Hold a clear glass sheet, a sheet of butter paper and a piece of cardboard in front of a lit torch one by one. Before you try, predict what you will see through each.
prompt_hi: Ek-ek karke saaf kaanch, butter paper aur gatte ko jalti torch ke saamne rakho. Karne se pehle guess karo har ek se kya dikhega.
answer: Glass: the torch is seen clearly (transparent). Butter paper: only a glow, not clearly (translucent). Cardboard: no light (opaque).

subject: science
prompt_en: In a dark room, shine a torch onto a steel bowl so that it 'shines'. Predict what happens to the bowl's brightness when you switch the torch off, and what this tells you about the Moon.
prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein torch steel ki katori pe daalo taaki woh chamke. Guess karo torch band karne pe katori ki chamak ka kya hoga, aur isse Chaand ke baare mein kya pata chalta hai.
answer: The bowl goes dark immediately, because it was only reflecting the torch's light; the Moon similarly shines only by reflecting sunlight.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why can you see this page, even though the page does not give out light?
prompt_hi: Ye page khud roshni nahi deta, phir bhi tum ise kaise dekh paate ho?
answer: Light from a source (a bulb or the Sun) falls on the page and is reflected into our eyes.

subject: science
prompt_en: Frosted glass is used in bathroom windows and clear glass in shop windows. Explain why using the words transparent and translucent.
prompt_hi: Bathroom ki khidki mein frosted glass aur dukaan ki khidki mein saaf glass lagaate hain. Transparent aur translucent shabdon se samjhao kyun.
answer: Frosted glass is translucent: it lets light in but people cannot see clearly through it, giving privacy; clear shop glass is transparent so customers can see the goods.

subject: science
prompt_en: Pooja says: 'The Moon is luminous because it is the brightest thing in the night sky.' Correct her.
prompt_hi: Pooja kehti hai: 'Chaand luminous hai kyunki raat ke aasmaan mein sabse chamakdaar hai.' Use sahi karo.
answer: Brightness does not make something luminous; the Moon does not make its own light, it reflects sunlight, so it is non-luminous.

subject: science
prompt_en: Classify: a clean plastic water bottle, a sheet of oiled paper, a wooden door, still pond water, a steel tiffin box.
prompt_hi: Classify karo: saaf plastic ki paani ki bottle, tel laga kaagaz, lakdi ka darwaaza, shaant taalaab ka saaf paani, steel ka tiffin.
answer: Transparent: clean plastic bottle, clean pond water (if clear). Translucent: oiled paper. Opaque: wooden door, steel tiffin.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw (or describe) arrows showing how you see a mango on the table in a room lit by a bulb.
prompt_hi: Bulb se roshan kamre mein mez pe rakha aam tum kaise dekhte ho, teer se dikhaao (ya batao).
answer: An arrow from the bulb to the mango, then an arrow from the mango to the eye: light from the bulb falls on the mango and is reflected into the eye.

subject: science
prompt_en: Fireflies glow on summer nights in villages, and some deep-sea fish glow too. Are they luminous or non-luminous? Why might glowing be useful to them?
prompt_hi: Garmi ki raaton mein gaon mein jugnu chamakte hain, aur kuch gehre samundar ki machhliyan bhi chamakti hain. Ye luminous hain ya non-luminous? Chamakna unke liye kyun useful ho sakta hai?
answer: Luminous, because they make their own light. Glowing can help them find mates, attract prey or communicate in the dark.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a friend the difference between transparent, translucent and opaque, with one example from your house for each.
prompt_hi: Dost ko transparent, translucent aur opaque ka farak samjhao, ghar se har ek ka ek example dekar.
answer: Key ideas: transparent lets almost all light pass so we see clearly (window glass); translucent lets some light pass but not clearly (butter paper, frosted glass); opaque lets no light pass (door, wall).

subject: science
prompt_en: From memory: give two examples of luminous objects.
prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: do luminous cheezon ke naam.
answer: Any two: Sun, stars, candle flame, lit bulb, firefly, glowing torch.

subject: science
prompt_en: In a dark room, hold your hand between a torch and the wall. Before you move it, predict: what happens to the shadow when you move your hand closer to the torch?
prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein torch aur deewar ke beech haath rakho. Hilaane se pehle guess karo: haath ko torch ke paas le jaane pe parchhaai ka kya hoga?
answer: The shadow gets bigger (and more blurred at the edges), because the hand blocks a wider cone of light.

subject: science
prompt_en: A green leaf and a black stone of similar size are held in front of a torch. Predict the colour of each shadow on a white wall.
prompt_hi: Ek hara patta aur ek kaala patthar, lagbhag ek size ke, torch ke saamne rakhe hain. Safed deewar pe dono ki parchhaai ka rang guess karo.
answer: Both shadows are dark; a shadow shows the shape, not the colour of the object.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why does a shadow form at all? Use the idea of how light travels.
prompt_hi: Parchhaai banti hi kyun hai? Roshni kaise chalti hai, us idea se batao.
answer: Light travels in straight lines and cannot bend around an opaque object, so the region behind the object gets no light and looks dark.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare your shadow on the ground and your image in a mirror: give three differences.
prompt_hi: Zameen pe tumhari parchhaai aur sheeshe mein tumhari image ki tulna karo: 3 farak batao.
answer: The shadow is dark and shows only the outline; the image shows colours and details. The shadow forms where light is blocked; the image forms by reflection. The shadow's size changes with distance from the source; the plane mirror image is the same size as you.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ravi writes: 'My shadow is my reflection on the ground.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Ravi likhta hai: 'Meri parchhaai zameen pe meri reflection hai.' Kya galat hai?
answer: A shadow is not a reflection; it is the dark area where his body blocks sunlight. A reflection needs light bouncing back from a shiny surface and would show colours and details.

subject: science
prompt_en: A cricket stump is fixed upright on the ground. How does its shadow on the ground change from morning to noon to evening on a sunny day?
prompt_hi: Ek cricket stump zameen pe seedha gada hai. Dhoop wale din subah, dopahar aur shaam ko uski parchhaai kaise badalti hai?
answer: Morning: long, pointing west (away from the Sun in the east). Noon: shortest (and in India it may point almost north). Evening: long again, pointing east.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw (or describe) a ray diagram: a torch, a ball, and a wall. Show the straight lines of light and where the shadow forms.
prompt_hi: Ek ray diagram banao (ya batao): torch, ball aur deewar. Roshni ki seedhi lines aur parchhaai kahaan banti hai dikhaao.
answer: Straight lines from the torch go past the top and bottom edges of the ball to the wall; the region on the wall between these two lines gets no light and is the shadow.

subject: science
prompt_en: In a traditional shadow-puppet show (like Tholu Bommalata of Andhra Pradesh), how does the puppeteer make a character seem to walk toward the audience and grow bigger?
prompt_hi: Paramparik shadow-puppet show mein (jaise Andhra Pradesh ka Tholu Bommalata), kalaakaar kirdaar ko darshakon ki taraf aata aur bada hota kaise dikhaata hai?
answer: By moving the puppet closer to the lamp and away from the screen, so the shadow on the screen grows; moving it back toward the screen shrinks it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how a shadow forms, why it is dark, and how to make it bigger.
prompt_hi: Chhote bachche ko samjhao parchhaai kaise banti hai, kaali kyun hoti hai, aur badi kaise karein.
answer: Key ideas: light travels in straight lines; an opaque object blocks light; the region behind gets no light so the shadow is dark; it shows shape not colour; moving the object closer to the source makes the shadow bigger.

subject: science
prompt_en: From memory: can a transparent sheet of glass make a dark shadow? Why or why not?
prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: kya saaf kaanch ki sheet kaali parchhaai bana sakti hai? Kyun ya kyun nahi?
answer: No (at most a very faint one), because it lets almost all light pass through; dark shadows need opaque objects.

subject: science
prompt_en: Write the word TAXI in capital letters on paper and hold it facing a mirror. Before you look, predict how it will appear.
prompt_hi: Kaagaz pe bade aksharon mein TAXI likho aur use sheeshe ki taraf rakho. Dekhne se pehle guess karo kaisa dikhega.
answer: It looks the same as TAXI, because T, A, X and I are symmetric left to right, so lateral inversion does not change how they look; a word like BUS would look reversed.

subject: science
prompt_en: You stand 1 metre in front of a mirror, then step back 1 more metre. Predict how far away your image now appears from you.
prompt_hi: Tum sheeshe se 1 meter door khade ho, phir 1 meter aur peeche hat jaate ho. Guess karo ab tumhari image tumse kitni door dikhegi.
answer: 4 metres: you are 2 m in front, and the image is 2 m behind the mirror.

subject: science
prompt_en: List three features of the image formed by a plane mirror.
prompt_hi: Plane mirror se bani image ki 3 visheshtaayein batao.
answer: Any three: upright; same size as the object; as far behind the mirror as the object is in front; laterally inverted; cannot be caught on a screen.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is AMBULANCE written in mirror writing on the front of an ambulance?
prompt_hi: Ambulance ke aage AMBULANCE ulta (mirror writing mein) kyun likha hota hai?
answer: So that drivers ahead, looking in their rear-view mirrors, see it laterally inverted back into the correct readable word and give way quickly.

subject: science
prompt_en: Dev says: 'In a mirror, my image is upside down because mirrors flip everything.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Dev kehta hai: 'Sheeshe mein meri image ulti (sir neeche) hoti hai kyunki sheesha sab palat deta hai.' Kya galat hai?
answer: A plane mirror image is upright; only left and right appear swapped (lateral inversion), not top and bottom.

subject: science
prompt_en: A ray of light strikes a mirror at 30° to the normal (the line perpendicular to the mirror). Draw (or describe) the reflected ray and give its angle.
prompt_hi: Ek prakash ki kiran mirror pe normal (mirror pe lamb rekha) se 30° ke kon pe padti hai. Paraavartit kiran banao (ya batao) aur uska kon do.
answer: The reflected ray leaves on the other side of the normal at 30°, because the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.

subject: science
prompt_en: Ria combs her hair with her right hand in front of a mirror. Which hand does her image seem to use, and why?
prompt_hi: Ria sheeshe ke saamne daahine haath se baal sanwaarti hai. Uski image kis haath ka use karti dikhti hai, aur kyun?
answer: The image seems to use its left hand, because a plane mirror laterally inverts the image, swapping left and right.

subject: science
prompt_en: A barber's shop has two mirrors on opposite walls, facing each other. Customers see many images going far back. Explain.
prompt_hi: Naai ki dukaan mein aamne-saamne deewaron pe do sheeshe hain. Graahakon ko bahut saari images door tak dikhti hain. Samjhao.
answer: Light reflects back and forth between the two parallel mirrors many times; each reflection forms another image farther behind, so a long row of images is seen, getting dimmer as some light is lost each time.

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a friend where your image is when you look into a plane mirror, and what is special about it.
prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki plane mirror mein dekhne pe tumhari image kahaan hoti hai, aur usmein kya khaas hai.
answer: Key ideas: the image appears behind the mirror, as far behind as you are in front; it is upright and the same size; left and right are swapped (lateral inversion); it cannot be caught on a screen.

subject: science
prompt_en: From memory: what is the swapping of left and right in a mirror image called?
prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: mirror image mein left aur right ka badal jaana kya kehlaata hai?
answer: Lateral inversion.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if you make the pinhole bigger, how will the image change?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: pinhole bada karne pe image kaise badlegi?
answer: It becomes brighter but blurred, because a big hole is like many small holes each making an image, and these overlap.

subject: science
prompt_en: In a periscope, the top mirror faces down at 45°. Predict what you would see if the top mirror were removed.
prompt_hi: Periscope mein upar wala sheesha 45° pe neeche ki taraf hai. Guess karo agar upar wala sheesha hata do toh kya dikhega.
answer: You would not see over the wall; you would only see the inside of the tube (or straight up through the top opening via the bottom mirror), because light from the scene is no longer reflected down.

subject: science
prompt_en: At what angle are the two mirrors in a periscope placed, and are they parallel to each other?
prompt_hi: Periscope mein dono sheeshe kis kon pe lagte hain, aur kya ek doosre ke parallel hote hain?
answer: Each at 45° to the tube, parallel to each other and facing each other.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is the image in a pinhole camera upside down?
prompt_hi: Pinhole camera mein image ulti kyun hoti hai?
answer: Light travels in straight lines: rays from the top of the object pass through the hole and reach the bottom of the screen, and rays from the bottom reach the top, so the image is inverted.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare the image in a plane mirror and in a pinhole camera: upright or inverted? Can it be seen on a screen?
prompt_hi: Plane mirror aur pinhole camera ki image ki tulna karo: seedhi ya ulti? Kya screen pe dikh sakti hai?
answer: Plane mirror: upright, cannot be caught on a screen. Pinhole camera: inverted, formed on the screen.
